IUT4.ThmA.content: Diophantine inequality for hyperbolic curves: the height of omega_X(D) is bounded, up to a bounded discrepancy, by (1 + epsilon) times the sum of the log-different and the log-conductor on points of bounded degree.
explicit_hypotheses: X a smooth, proper, geometrically connected curve over a number field
D a reduced divisor, U_X = X minus D hyperbolic (deg omega_X(D) > 0)
d a positive integer, epsilon a positive real
implicit_hypotheses: heights, log-differents, log-conductors in the sense of [GenEll], Definitions 1.2 and 1.5
the relation <~ in the corrected sense of Remark 2.3.1 (ii)
IUT4.ThmA.conclusion: ht_{omega_X(D)} <~ (1 + epsilon)(log-diff_X + log-cond_D) on U_X(Qbar)^{<= d}.
obligations: Theorem A is Corollary 2.3; see that record.
The specialization to the abc inequality (X = P^1, D = {0, 1, infinity}, d = 1) is described in docs/PAPER_IV_DERIVATION.md and is not formalized.

IUT4.Prop1_1.content: Multiple tensor products and differents. For a fixed index * in I and I* = I minus {*}, the normalization (R_I)^~ of the tensor product R_I = tensor over Z_p of the R_i satisfies p^{d_{I*}} (R_I)^~ inside R_I inside (R_I)^~, where d_{I*} is the sum of the orders d_i of the differents over i in I*.
explicit_hypotheses: p a prime number; I a finite set of cardinality >= 2
for i in I, k_i a finite extension of Q_p inside an algebraic closure of Q_p, R_i its ring of integers, d_i in Q_{>=0} the order of a generator of the different ideal of R_i over Z_p
for nonempty E in I: R_E = tensor product over Z_p of the R_i (i in E), d_E = sum of d_i (i in E)
a fixed element * of I, and I* = I minus {*}
implicit_hypotheses: ord is the p-adic valuation normalized by ord(p) = 1; p^lambda denotes an unspecified element of order lambda
(-)^~ is the normalization of the reduced ring in its ring of fractions
IUT4.Prop1_1.conclusion: p^{d_{I*}} (R_I)^~ is contained in R_I, which is contained in (R_I)^~; the left-hand side is well defined for suitable p^{d_{I*}}, for example products of elements p^{d_i} of R_i (i in I*).
definitions_required: R_I = tensor product of the R_i over Z_p
obligations: Not formalized: needs tensor products of p-adic rings of integers and their normalizations, which Mathlib does not provide in this form.

IUT4.Prop1_2.content: Defines a_i = (1/e_i) ceil(e_i/(p-2)) (p > 2), a_i = 2 (p = 2), b_i = floor(log(p e_i/(p-1))/log p) − 1/e_i, and bounds p-adic logarithms of unit groups and automorphisms of their tensor products by powers of p.

e_i the ramification index of k_i over Q_p
phi an automorphism of the Q_p-vector space log_p(R_I^x) tensor Q_p that induces an automorphism of the submodule log_p(R_I^x)
lambda in (1/e_i) Z, i in I (in (ii), (iii))
(iii): p > 2 and e_i <= p - 2 for all i; (iv): p > 2 and e_i = 1 for all i
IUT4.Prop1_2.conclusion: (i) p^{a_i} R_i in log_p(R_i^x) in p^{-b_i} R_i, with equalities if p > 2 and e_i <= p-2; (ii) phi(p^lambda (R_I)^~) in p^{floor(lambda - d_I - a_I)} log_p(R_I^x) in p^{floor(lambda - d_I - a_I) - b_I} (R_I)^~; (iii) phi(p^lambda (R_I)^~) in p^{lambda - d_I - 1} (R_I)^~; (iv) phi((R_I)^~) in (R_I)^~.

IUT4.Prop1_5.content: Archimedean metric estimates: C tensor_R C = C + C is compatible with metrics up to a factor 2; primitive automorphisms preserve decompositions; M_I splits into 2^{|I|-1}|V|^{|I|} copies of C with metric factor 2^{|I|-1}; tensor products of vectors of length lambda lie in lambda^{|I|} B_I.
explicit_hypotheses: C with its standard Hermitian metric; primitive automorphisms generated by complex conjugation and multiplication by +-1, +-sqrt(-1)
(iii), (iv): I, V nonempty finite sets; M = direct sum of copies C_v (v in V); M_I = tensor product over R of copies M_i of M; B_I the product of unit balls
(iv): lambda > 0 and m_i in M_i whose components have length lambda
IUT4.Prop1_5.conclusion: (i) C tensor_R C = C + C is compatible with the metrics up to a factor 2; (ii) the decomposition is preserved by primitive automorphisms; (iii) M_I is a direct sum of 2^{|I|-1}|V|^{|I|} copies of C, with direct sum metric 2^{|I|-1} times the tensor metric, and B_I is preserved; (iv) the tensor product of the m_i lies in lambda^{|I|} B_I.
obligations: Tensor product metrics, the primitive automorphisms of (ii), the metric factor and integral structure of (iii) and the inclusion of (iv) are not formalized.

IUT4.Def3_3.conclusion: Definitions of mutations, composition and identity mutations, morphisms and isomorphisms of mutations, mutation-equivalences (with the observation that for 1-small species they induce bijections on species-morphisms and species-isomorphisms), mutation-histories, observables and cores.
